etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English careful, from Old English carful; equivalent to care +‎ -ful.

definitions.definition: Taking care; attentive to potential danger, error or harm; cautious.

quote.citation: 2019, Li Huang, James Lambert, “Another Arrow for the Quiver: A New Methodology for Multilingual Researchers”, in Journal of Multilingual and Multicultural Development, →DOI, page 7:
quote.text: At the same time, we were cognisant that careful scholars should never solely rely on their own impressionistic observations, and, that our own impressions were inexact and not capable of being quantified.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) Full of care or grief; sorrowful, sad.
(obsolete) Full of cares or anxiety; worried, troubled.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book III, Canto I”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: Where through long watch, and late daies weary toile, / She soundly slept, and carefull thoughts did quite assoile.
